\section{Canonical equations and typed operators}
\label{sec:equations}

The exact spherical equations in this section are mathematical identities and
the independent offline oracle.  The v0.1 production geometry may retain the
established small-angle operator only inside the preregistered adequacy domain
defined in Section~\ref{sec:assumptions}; no automatic spherical fallback or
universal numerical threshold is implied.

\subsection{Directions, tangent basis, and circular topology}

For longitude $\ell$ and latitude $b$ in a declared frame,
\begin{equation}
 \widehat{\boldsymbol u}_{\rm sky}(\ell,b)=
 \begin{bmatrix}\cos b\cos\ell\\ \cos b\sin\ell\\ \sin b\end{bmatrix},
 \quad
 \boldsymbol e_\ell=
 \begin{bmatrix}-\sin\ell\\ \cos\ell\\0\end{bmatrix},
 \quad
 \boldsymbol e_b=
 \begin{bmatrix}-\sin b\cos\ell\\-\sin b\sin\ell\\\cos b\end{bmatrix}.
 \label{eq:unit-basis}
\end{equation}
Away from a coordinate pole, $\boldsymbol e_\ell$ and $\boldsymbol e_b$ are
unit tangent vectors toward increasing longitude at fixed latitude and
increasing latitude.  The direction remains
$\widehat{\boldsymbol u}_{\rm sky}$ at a pole.  The symbols $x$ and $r$ are
reserved for paired KID readout coordinates and never denote sky vectors or
TAN axes.

For period $P$,
\begin{align}
 \operatorname{wrap}_P(\theta)
 &=\theta-P\left\lfloor\frac{\theta+P/2}{P}\right\rfloor
   \in[-P/2,P/2),\label{eq:wrap}\\
 \operatorname{norm}_P(\theta)
 &=\theta-P\left\lfloor\frac{\theta}{P}\right\rfloor
   \in[0,P).\label{eq:norm}
\end{align}
Longitude and azimuth use $P=2\pi$.  The half-open endpoint convention is
deterministic.  Exactly antipodal samples have no unique shortest interpolation
path; interpolation is unavailable unless an explicit unwrap authority names
and parents the selected path.

\subsection{Exact displacement oracle and input normalization}

For tangent components
$\boldsymbol\eta=(\eta_1,\eta_2)^\mathsf T$ in the local orthonormal basis
$(\boldsymbol e_1,\boldsymbol e_2)$, define
$\boldsymbol t=\eta_1\boldsymbol e_1+\eta_2\boldsymbol e_2$,
$\rho=\lVert\boldsymbol t\rVert$ and, for $\rho>0$,
$\widehat{\boldsymbol v}=\boldsymbol t/\rho$.  The exact spherical displacement oracle is
\begin{equation}
 \operatorname{Exp}_{\widehat{\boldsymbol u}_{\rm sky}}(\boldsymbol\eta)=
 \begin{cases}
  \cos\rho\,\widehat{\boldsymbol u}_{\rm sky}
   +\sin\rho\,\widehat{\boldsymbol v},&\rho>0,\\
  \widehat{\boldsymbol u}_{\rm sky},&\rho=0.
 \end{cases}
 \label{eq:exp}
\end{equation}
Renormalization may remove roundoff only; it may not hide invalid input.

An input longitude-like component is normalized at the boundary as
\begin{equation}
 \eta_\ell=
 \begin{cases}
  \cos b\,\Delta\ell,&\text{declared coordinate increment},\\
  \Delta\ell_{\rm tangent},&\text{declared on-sky tangent component}.
 \end{cases}
 \label{eq:longitude-normalization}
\end{equation}
The declared correction pair $\boldsymbol a_k$ in arcseconds becomes
\begin{equation}
 \boldsymbol c_k=\kappa\boldsymbol a_k.
 \label{eq:correction-unit}
\end{equation}
Positive components move toward the increasing declared tangent-basis axes.
An upstream residual requiring the opposite action needs one explicit,
parented sign adapter and an application count of one.

\subsection{Pointing-support realization}

One finite pair is constant:
\begin{equation}
 \boldsymbol c_s=\boldsymbol c_0.
 \label{eq:constant-correction}
\end{equation}
For two finite, strictly increasing MJD supports $m_0<m_1$ and aligned
stable-slot occurrence time $m_s$,
\begin{equation}
 \lambda_s=\frac{m_s-m_0}{m_1-m_0},\qquad
 \boldsymbol c_s=(1-\lambda_s)\boldsymbol c_0+
                  \lambda_s\boldsymbol c_1,
 \qquad 0\leq\lambda_s\leq1.
 \label{eq:mjd-correction}
\end{equation}
For explicit legacy observation-span mode, where $t_-$ and $t_+$ are the
times of the exact first and last admitted aligned sample identities,
\begin{equation}
 \lambda_s^{\rm span}=\frac{t_s-t_-}{t_+-t_-},\qquad
 \boldsymbol c_s=(1-\lambda_s^{\rm span})\boldsymbol c_0+
                  \lambda_s^{\rm span}\boldsymbol c_1,
 \quad t_-\leq t_s\leq t_+.
 \label{eq:span-correction}
\end{equation}
A one-sample span is defined only when the endpoint corrections are exactly
equal, in which case Equation~\ref{eq:constant-correction} applies.

When the two-support covariance is available, stack
$\boldsymbol c_*=(\boldsymbol c_0^\mathsf T,
\boldsymbol c_1^\mathsf T)^\mathsf T$ and define
\begin{equation}
 \mathsf H_s=
 \begin{bmatrix}(1-\lambda_s)\mathsf I_2&\lambda_s\mathsf I_2\end{bmatrix},
 \quad
 \mathsf C_{c,s}^{\rm formal}=
 \mathsf H_s\mathsf C_{c,*}\mathsf H_s^\mathsf T.
 \label{eq:support-covariance}
\end{equation}
Cross-covariance is retained when supplied.  Model, selection, and systematic
terms remain separately labeled.

\subsection{Ordered detector-direction composition}

Let $\widehat{\boldsymbol u}^{B}_{\rm sky,s}$ be the exact aligned boresight in the declared native
horizon frame.  The spherical oracle for the first two geometric stages is
\begin{align}
 \widehat{\boldsymbol u}^{H,c}_{\rm sky,s}
   &=\operatorname{Exp}_{\widehat{\boldsymbol u}^{B}_{\rm sky,s}}
     (\boldsymbol c_s),
   \label{eq:corrected-boresight}\\
 \boldsymbol\xi_{ds}
   &=\mathcal G_\gamma(\boldsymbol g_d;t_s,E_s,
      \text{declared occurrence-local state}),
   \label{eq:geometry-realization}\\
 \widehat{\boldsymbol u}^{H}_{\rm sky,ds}
   &=\mathcal C_\gamma(\widehat{\boldsymbol u}^{H,c}_{\rm sky,s},
      \boldsymbol\xi_{ds}),
   \label{eq:detector-direction}\\
 \widehat{\boldsymbol u}^{F}_{\rm sky,ds}
   &=\mathsf R_{F\leftarrow H,s}
      (\widehat{\boldsymbol u}^{H}_{\rm sky,ds}).
   \label{eq:frame-operation}
\end{align}
$\mathcal C_\gamma$ is the selected composition relation and carries the same
gauge, pivot, basis, handedness, affine limitations, and lineage as
$\mathcal G_\gamma$.  In the admitted pure tangent-displacement limiting
case, $\mathcal C_\gamma(\widehat{\boldsymbol u}_{\rm sky},\boldsymbol\xi)=
\operatorname{Exp}_{\widehat{\boldsymbol u}_{\rm sky}}(\boldsymbol\xi)$; the contract does not
presume that this limiting case describes every selected artifact.

The established production small-angle relation may be written
\begin{equation}
 \boldsymbol\eta_{ds}^{\rm prod}\simeq
 \boldsymbol c_s+\mathsf B_{ds}\boldsymbol f_d,
 \label{eq:small-angle}
\end{equation}
only when $\mathsf B_{ds}$ is the declared selected geometry/rotation mapping
and the preregistered adequacy record admits the exact occurrence, detector,
product use, and error metric.  Equation~\ref{eq:exp} and the full selected
geometry relation are the offline oracle for that record.

\subsection{Gnomonic projection}

For output direction $\widehat{\boldsymbol u}_{\rm sky}$, center
$\widehat{\boldsymbol u}_{\rm sky,0}$, and center
basis $(\boldsymbol e_1,\boldsymbol e_2)$,
\begin{equation}
 D=\widehat{\boldsymbol u}_{\rm sky}\!\cdot\!
   \widehat{\boldsymbol u}_{\rm sky,0},\qquad
 \zeta_1=\frac{\widehat{\boldsymbol u}_{\rm sky}\cdot\boldsymbol e_1}{D},
 \qquad
 \zeta_2=\frac{\widehat{\boldsymbol u}_{\rm sky}\cdot\boldsymbol e_2}{D},
 \qquad D>0.
 \label{eq:tan-forward}
\end{equation}
The inverse is
\begin{equation}
 \widehat{\boldsymbol u}_{\rm sky}=
 \frac{\widehat{\boldsymbol u}_{\rm sky,0}
       +\zeta_1\boldsymbol e_1+\zeta_2\boldsymbol e_2}
      {\sqrt{1+\zeta_1^2+\zeta_2^2}}.
 \label{eq:tan-inverse}
\end{equation}
In longitude and latitude, with
$\Delta\ell=\operatorname{wrap}_{2\pi}(\ell-\ell_0)$,
\begin{align}
 D&=\sin b_0\sin b+\cos b_0\cos b\cos\Delta\ell,\nonumber\\
 \zeta_1&=\frac{\cos b\sin\Delta\ell}{D},\qquad
 \zeta_2=\frac{\cos b_0\sin b-
          \sin b_0\cos b\cos\Delta\ell}{D}.
 \label{eq:tan-lonlat}
\end{align}
The mathematical domain is finite $D>0$.  There is no universal positive
$D_{\min}$.  A separately preregistered footprint bound may be tighter, but
does not alter the mathematical domain.  Non-finite input or output and
$D\leq0$ are coordinate invalidity, never a center or edge pixel.

For Point/OOF/Beammap,
\begin{equation}
 \boldsymbol w=206264.806247\,(\zeta_1,\zeta_2)^\mathsf T\ \text{arcsec},
 \label{eq:altaz-plane}
\end{equation}
with ordered AZOFFSET/ELOFFSET identity.  For Science,
\begin{equation}
 \boldsymbol w=\frac{180}{\pi}(\zeta_1,\zeta_2)^\mathsf T\ \text{degree},
 \label{eq:science-plane}
\end{equation}
with explicitly identified RA---TAN/DEC--TAN axes in the declared equatorial
J2000 frame.

\subsection{Continuous WCS and nominal discrete pixel}

Let $\boldsymbol q_0=\mathrm{CRPIX}$ be one-based and let $\mathsf M$ be the
declared nonsingular CD matrix in plane-units per pixel:
\begin{equation}
 \boldsymbol w=\mathsf M(\boldsymbol q-\boldsymbol q_0),\qquad
 \boldsymbol q=\boldsymbol q_0+\mathsf M^{-1}\boldsymbol w.
 \label{eq:wcs}
\end{equation}
When the product plan places the projection center at the geometric array
center for $N_1$ columns and $N_2$ rows,
\begin{equation}
 \mathrm{CRPIX}_1=\frac{N_1+1}{2},\qquad
 \mathrm{CRPIX}_2=\frac{N_2+1}{2}.
 \label{eq:crpix}
\end{equation}
Even dimensions therefore have half-integer reference pixels.  A different
declared reference-pixel policy remains valid only when Equation~\ref{eq:wcs}
places CRVAL there exactly and provenance records that policy.

At pixel centers,
\begin{equation}
 q_1=h+1,\qquad q_2=j+1.
 \label{eq:index-base}
\end{equation}
The v0.1 half-open nearest-center assignment is
\begin{equation}
 h=\left\lfloor q_1-\tfrac12\right\rfloor,\qquad
 j=\left\lfloor q_2-\tfrac12\right\rfloor,
 \quad 0\leq h<N_1,\quad0\leq j<N_2.
 \label{eq:pixel-assignment}
\end{equation}
Another rule is a separately identified operator with equivalent boundary
tests; it is never inferred from integer casting.

\subsection{Typed map-center Jacobian and covariance}

For Equation~\ref{eq:tan-forward}, let
$a=\widehat{\boldsymbol u}_{\rm sky}\cdot\boldsymbol e_1$ and
$b=\widehat{\boldsymbol u}_{\rm sky}\cdot\boldsymbol e_2$.  The
direction-to-plane derivative is
\begin{equation}
 \mathsf J_{w\leftarrow u_{\rm sky}}=
 \begin{bmatrix}
 (D\boldsymbol e_1^\mathsf T-a\widehat{\boldsymbol u}_{\rm sky,0}^\mathsf T)/D^2\\
 (D\boldsymbol e_2^\mathsf T-b\widehat{\boldsymbol u}_{\rm sky,0}^\mathsf T)/D^2
 \end{bmatrix},
 \label{eq:projection-jacobian}
\end{equation}
followed by the declared unit conversion.  For a family-requested typed input
$\boldsymbol c_{\rm in}$ and output $\boldsymbol c_{\rm out}$,
\begin{equation}
 J_{\rm AST,0}^{({\rm out}\leftarrow{\rm in})}
 =\left.\frac{\partial\boldsymbol c_{\rm out}}
                {\partial\boldsymbol c_{\rm in}}\right|_{\widehat{\boldsymbol u}_{\rm sky,0},
                \mathcal W_o}.
 \label{eq:map-center-jacobian}
\end{equation}
Its direction, axes, units, family, center/WCS parent, approximation domain,
method, and included or unavailable terms are part of the type.  For an available
map-center covariance term $k$,
\begin{equation}
 \mathsf C_{\rm out}^{(k)}=
 J_{{\rm out}\leftarrow k}\mathsf C_k
 J_{{\rm out}\leftarrow k}^{\mathsf T}.
 \label{eq:center-covariance}
\end{equation}
Supplied cross terms are propagated.  No total is reported unless all claimed
components, cross-covariances, and combination assumptions are declared.

\subsection{Grid roles, RTC response, and delegated MAP operator}

On the ALIGN grid and the RTC output grid, respectively,
\begin{align}
 \theta^A_{ds}
   &=\mathcal A_{\rm AST}(d,s;\Pi^{A,{\rm role}}_{ds}),
   \label{eq:theta-align}\\
 \theta^{\rm RTC}_{dn}
   &=\mathcal A_{\rm AST}(d,n;\Pi^{\rm RTC}_{dn}).
   \label{eq:theta-rtc}
\end{align}
The second relation has stable product-role identity
\texttt{SCI-AST:rtc\_output\_grid\_coordinates@1}.  It is realized by AST for
every ordinary downstream science product whose numerical signal is
represented on an RTC output grid, and it binds the RTC-supplied parent in
Equation~\ref{eq:rtc-parent} without reconstruction.
For an RTC signal relation
\begin{equation}
 y_{dn}=\sum_s L_{ns}x_{ds},
 \label{eq:rtc-signal}
\end{equation}
the sky response retains $L_{ns}$ and the full set
$\{\theta^A_{ds}\}$ jointly.  In general,
\begin{equation}
 \text{sky-response}(L_{ns},\{\theta^A_{ds}\})
 \neq \sum_s L_{ns}\theta^A_{ds}.
 \label{eq:not-angular-filter}
\end{equation}

Before a complete MAP estimator request, the base AST geometry facts are only
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal B^{\rm AST}_{i}=
 (\boldsymbol q_i,\ [\text{nominal containing pixel}]_{\rm if\ requested},
 \ \text{bounds state}),
 \label{eq:geometry-incidence}
\end{equation}
with exact coordinate/WCS parent.  It contains no neighbor stencil or
candidate support whose extent depends on MAP kernel family or radius,
deposition support, edge policy, normalization, or conservation behavior, and
it has no numerical-contribution, MAP-support, response, covariance,
normalization, or estimator-validity meaning.

When and only when a complete exact MAP plan $\Pi^{\rm MAP}$ requests it, a
delegated $G_{pi}$ materialization has the typed parent relation
\begin{equation}
 G_{pi}^{\rm materialized}=
 \mathcal M_{\rm AST}\!\left(
   \Pi^{\rm AST}_{i},\mathcal W_o,
   [\Pi^{\rm RTC}_{i}]_{\rm if\ applicable},
   \Pi^{\rm MAP}_{\rm kernel/support/boundary/normalization}
 \right).
 \label{eq:gpi-parentage}
\end{equation}
$\mathcal M_{\rm AST}$ denotes a materialization service, not scientific
selection or ownership of $G_{pi}$.  Thus AST determines exactly where the
occurrence is, while MAP determines exactly how it contributes to pixels.
